## Report: `region.fasta` (region_001, 3,000 bp)

**General composition.** 3,000 nt, GC content 50.9% (uniform across the region — the 600 bp blocks range 48–53%, so no local GC islands or abrupt composition shifts). Even base usage (A 24.2%, T 24.9%, G 24.2%, C 26.7%), K-mer frequencies unremarkable, longest homopolymer run is only 5 bp, and stop-codon density (96 per ~1,000 triplets, split fairly evenly between TGA/TAA/TAG) is at random background. Nothing suggests repeats, mobile elements, low-complexity tracts, or rRNA/pseudo-gene character.

**Notable feature: a single long open reading frame on the lower strand.** The main finding is an intact ORF:

- Position (1-based, minus strand): 1050–2336; on the plus strand this corresponds to **~662–2951** (i.e., the ORF is encoded on the reverse strand of the sequence as given).
- Length: **428 codons → 428 aa protein**, ~47.9 kDa, predicted pI ≈ 5.4 (mildly acidic), no transmembrane-like hydrophobic stretch (longest hydrophobic run is only 4 aa — likely a soluble, cytosolic protein).
- It is bordered at both ends by in-frame stop codons, and the two remaining stop codons are absent — statistically striking and consistent with true coding sequence.
- One caveat: the ATG start falls directly at the sequence edge of interest ("...TACATG..." upstream: an AGG-rich triplet sits 8–11 nt upstream at rc coords 1039–1041 but is not a clean Shine-Dalgarno box, so the exact start (428 vs. 424 aa variant beginning at rc 1062, also on the minus strand) is ambiguous.

**Protein character.** A moderately sized acidic soluble protein. A few recurring motifs, including a C-terminal cysteine pair pattern (≈ residues 420–428: **NYCLICWK**, a Cxxx C motif) and a cysteine-rich core around residues 42, 61, 120, 189, 330 — but no unusually dense motif that I could tie to any canonical protein family.

**Bottom line:** the sequence contains one strong, intact 1.3-kbp protein-coding ORF on the reverse strand, spanning approximately residues 662–2951 of the 3,000 nt region, it encodes a ~48 kDa soluble acidic protein whose 5'-start is ambiguous (428 or 424 aa versions), and the flanking regions (~200 nt at each end plus ~100 nt internal gap at the top strand orientations) are compositionally unremarkable with no repeats or regulatory element signatures to report. Without database matching I cannot assign a function to the protein.
